headline: Beau Lamarre-Condon tells double murder trial shooting of Jesse Baird wasn’t intentional but ‘it was my fault’

members.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon trial live updates: former police officer continues evidence in double murder trial
members.lead: Lamarre-Condon says he shot his gun in the Royal national park to test the volume Lamarre-Condon tells the jury about an occasion when he went to the Royal national park with a friend and shot his gun. At this time he was thinking of taking his own life, and he wanted to test how loud his gun was, he told the jury. He says he fired it at a tree: I was very aware of making sure the bullet didn’t hit any innocent person. Police normally wear eye protection when firing their gun, Lamarre-Condon told the court, so when particulate entered his eyes from the shot, he said: “Shit there’s stuff in my eyes” and began rubbing it. He then retrieved a brown paper bag and put it over the firearm before firing a second shot, he told the jury. A little paper bag like that would never change the sound of a gun shot. members.lead: Former NSW police officer gives evidence for a second day after pleading not guilty to murdering Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024 Beau Lamarre-Condon trial live updates: former police officer continues evidence in double murder trial Beau Lamarre-Condon has said he is “guilty of manslaughter” but said shooting Jesse Baird wasn’t intentional, as he gave evidence in his double-murder trial. The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and his partner, Luke Davies, with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home in Sydney on 19 February 2024.
